name: Banking
description: Bank statement import and reconciliation -- the #1 practical anti-fraud control, and the one place a third party's independent record enters the system (plan/bank-import-reconciliation-spec.md). The posture is evidence handling, not ETL: bank_lines are append-only, keep their original row verbatim in `raw`, and are never hand-edited, so nobody can quietly reshape the evidence to agree with the books. Imports check THEMSELVES -- a statement carries its own checksum, so tie-out (opening + lines == closing) and continuity (this opening == the last statement's closing) run at import time and set the import's status; flagged imports still store their lines because hiding a truncated statement is exactly the failure this control catches, and the flags record which checks RAN so a balance-less CSV never reads as trustworthy as a tied-out one. Dedup is by the bank's own transaction id when the format has one (OFX FITID), else an ordinal-disambiguated content hash so genuine same-day twins both land while a re-imported file adds nothing; file-level idempotency is by sha256 of the statement itself. Reading a bank's export is DATA (bank_import_profiles.column_map), authored once with AI help and executed deterministically thereafter -- an AI that re-reads statements every month is nondeterministic and unauditable, the opposite of a control. Pure parsing/hashing/gate logic lives in object_banking.py at the repository root, a plain importable library like object_stock.py and object_finance.py, not a registered object. 0.1.0 shipped the evidence layer (collections, the CSV importer, the duplicate gate). 0.2.0 adds the reconciliation work itself: system_bank_matcher proposes book-side records for unmatched lines in tiers (reference+amount, exact amount in a date window, batched-deposit combinations) but only ever SUGGESTS above the configured auto-match tier, because confirming a match must be an ordinary attributed update -- reconciliation performed invisibly by whoever moves the money is the classic fraud hole. hook_bank_lines additionally makes the evidence immutable on update: what the bank said (posted_on, amount, description, raw, identity fields) can never be edited, only the operator's own reconciliation work can. action_resolve_bank_line books the unmatched tail -- bank fees and interest (entries small books routinely never record, which is why their cash drifts until they stop reconciling), own-account transfers, and NSF bounces -- each through object_finance.compose_posted_journal stamped generated_from bank_lines/{id} so resolving twice composes once. The reconciliation statement view is the remaining slice. 0.3.0 adds two things. `value_accounts` generalizes bank_accounts to every place value actually sits -- a checking account, a hardware wallet, a till, a gift card -- carrying denomination, custody (institution/self/third_party), how the balance can be VERIFIED, who manages it day to day, and whether a count needs a witness; the assurance a reconciliation carries follows from the verification method rather than being assumed equal (object_money.assurance_for). value_accounts REPLACED bank_accounts outright in 0.4.0 (rename plus a richer shape, migrated in one commit rather than left as two collections for one concept -- the drift this project criticises in the predecessor). And system_bank_escalation turns a quietly growing unreconciled tail into work someone is accountable for, in BOTH directions: bank lines the books cannot explain, and -- the direction people forget, and the more serious one -- recorded payments the bank never confirmed. OFX/QFX import lands too (action_import_ofx over object_ofx.py): the format worth supporting after CSV because it carries a stable per-transaction id (FITID), which makes dedup exact rather than heuristic and survives a bank re-wording a memo, and a stated closing balance, which lets the statement check its own arithmetic. OFX has no opening-balance tag at all, so a chained opening is taken from the previous statement's closing -- and the import records that the figure was DERIVED, because it makes the continuity check true by construction and only tie-out then carries weight. 0.4.0 also reconciles the accounts nobody sends a statement for: action_record_count counts a till or a safe, stamps what the books said at that moment, books the variance as cash over/short (a real expense -- pretending the drawer always balances is how a slow leak stays invisible for years), and records who counted AND who witnessed. An account may refuse a self-certified count outright, because the person counting the till is usually the person who could take from it. Structurally the same verb as app-catalog's action_apply_count: inventory shrinkage and a cash shortage are the same event in different denominations.

schedules.description: Suggest and auto-match bank lines against existing records.
Escalate bank lines left unmatched too long, so a stalled reconciliation is visible rather than silent.
